questions.stem: What does a reference architecture provide?
options: A detailed, project-specific design customised for a single solution
A high-level diagram representing the structural pattern of a solution, giving a consistent framework for similar projects across an organisation
A list of every server and its IP address
A budget forecast for a technology programme
A record of past project failures
questions.explanation: Reference architecture is a high-level diagram of a solution's structural pattern that establishes a consistent framework guiding the design and implementation of similar projects across an organisation.

questions.stem: How does a reference architecture differ from a solution architecture?
options: Reference architecture is customised for each project; solution architecture is generic
They are identical documents produced at different times
Reference architecture is a generalised template aligned with best practices, while solution architecture is customised for each project
Solution architecture is only for business stakeholders; reference architecture only for engineers
Reference architecture covers hardware only; solution architecture covers software only
questions.explanation: Unlike solution architecture, which is tailored to each project, reference architecture offers a generalised, best-practice template that is broadly applicable.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a benefit of a reference architecture?
options: Ensuring consistency across solutions
Reducing redundancy
Accelerating solution delivery with a clear blueprint
Eliminating the need for any data governance
Aiding risk management through tried-and-tested design patterns
questions.explanation: Reference architecture ensures consistency, reduces redundancy, accelerates delivery and supports risk management. It does not remove governance; in fact a data governance layer is one of its key components.

questions.stem: In a data and AI cognitive (DAC) reference architecture, what is the role of the landing zone?
options: A centralised area where raw data is ingested and stored temporarily, acting as a buffer before more structured layers
The final layer where dashboards and reports are delivered to users
The layer where machine learning models are trained
A logical view of data that avoids physically moving it
The layer that enforces regulations and audit logs
questions.explanation: The landing zone is where raw data is ingested and held temporarily, providing secure, controlled intake from diverse sources while maintaining integrity and traceability.

questions.stem: In a DAC reference architecture, in which component does data undergo preliminary cleaning and transformation to ensure consistency and completeness before advancing through the pipeline?
options: Data sources
Presentation and consumption layer
Virtualization layer
Analytics and machine learning layer
Staging area
questions.explanation: After ingestion, data moves to the staging area, where it receives preliminary cleaning and transformation in preparation for further processing.

questions.stem: What does the virtualization layer of a reference architecture provide?
options: Physical copies of every dataset on each analyst's machine
A logical view of data for direct access without physically moving or duplicating it
Temporary storage for raw ingested files
Executive dashboards and APIs
Audit logs and security controls
questions.explanation: The virtualization layer offers a logical view of data so it can be accessed directly without being moved or duplicated, optimising resources and supporting diverse queries.

questions.stem: Which layer of a DAC reference architecture incorporates data quality, metadata management, security controls and audit logs to maintain compliance and trustworthiness?
options: Transformation and storage layer
Landing zone
Data governance layer
Virtualization layer
Staging area
questions.explanation: The data governance layer ensures data usage adheres to regulations, standards and policies through data quality, metadata management, security controls and audit logs.

questions.stem: Data scientists building predictive models and applying deep learning, NLP and real-time analytics are working in which layer of a reference architecture?
options: Analytics and machine learning layer
Landing zone
Data sources
Presentation and consumption layer
Staging area
questions.explanation: The analytics and machine learning layer houses analytics, ML and AI workloads where specialists experiment, build predictive models and apply techniques such as deep learning and NLP.

questions.stem: Which tools are named as examples that may populate the presentation layer of a cloud-centric reference architecture?
options: Azure Data Factory and Google BigQuery
Amazon Redshift and Google BigQuery
Tableau, Power BI or custom web applications
MySQL and PostgreSQL
MongoDB and Cassandra
questions.explanation: Tableau, Power BI or custom web applications are cited as presentation-layer tools, whereas Azure Data Factory, Google BigQuery and Amazon Redshift are named for storage and transformation.

questions.stem: From a business perspective, how does a reference architecture serve stakeholders?
options: It replaces the need for any technical team
It provides line-by-line code for developers
It sets the pricing of the final product
It acts as a communication bridge between technical teams and business stakeholders, giving a shared understanding of the solution's structure and strategic objectives
It restricts access to technical diagrams to engineers only
questions.explanation: Reference architecture lets stakeholders grasp complex technical workflows without deep technical knowledge, serving as a communication bridge and creating shared understanding.
